items.followUp: State two properties of a liquid suitable for use in a thermometer.

rubric.why: Awards the mark for identifying a thermometer as an instrument used to measure temperature.
rubric.how: State that a thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature.

rubric.why: Uniform expansion makes the liquid's change in length correspond reliably to temperature change.
rubric.description: Gives uniform expansion as a useful property.
rubric.how: State that the liquid expands uniformly when its temperature changes.

rubric.why: These properties allow the liquid to measure a wide range of temperatures.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable temperature range property.
rubric.how: State that the liquid has a high boiling point or a low freezing point.

rubric.why: These are other useful properties that make the liquid easy to read or sensitive to temperature changes.
rubric.description: Gives another suitable property of the liquid.
rubric.how: State that it does not wet glass, is visible, or has a high coefficient of expansion.

modelAnswer: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature.
The liquid used in a thermometer should expand uniformly with temperature.
It should have a high boiling point and a low freezing point.
It should be visible and should not wet the glass.

items.followUp: A force of 30 N acts on a square surface of side 20 mm. Calculate the pressure on the surface.

rubric.why: The force is needed to apply the pressure formula.
rubric.how: Write the given force as 20 N.

rubric.why: Converts the side length into SI units before finding area.
rubric.description: Converts the side length to metres.
rubric.how: Write the side as 10 mm = 0.01 m.

rubric.why: The area of the square is its side multiplied by itself.
rubric.description: Finds the area of the square.
rubric.how: Use A = side² to obtain 1 × 10⁻⁴ m².

rubric.why: Pressure is force divided by area; the result is expressed in pascals.
rubric.description: Calculates pressure with the correct unit.
rubric.how: Substitute into P = F/A and give the answer in Pa.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 20 N, side = 10 mm = 0.01 m.
Area, A = side² = (0.01 m)² = 1 × 10⁻⁴ m².
Formula: P = F/A.
Substitution: P = 20 N / (1 × 10⁻⁴ m²) = 2 × 10⁵ N/m².
Answer: Pressure = 2 × 10⁵ Pa.

items.followUp: Name two factors that affect the accuracy of a measurement.

rubric.why: Instrument resolution or sensitivity affects how precisely a value can be measured.
rubric.how: Name the least count or sensitivity/quality of the measuring instrument.

rubric.why: The observer's skill and care affect the reading taken.
rubric.how: Name the skill, experience, or care of the observer.

modelAnswer: Accuracy in measuring a physical quantity depends on the least count (or sensitivity) of the measuring instrument.
It also depends on the skill and care of the observer.

items.followUp: Define a derived unit and give two examples.

rubric.why: A derived unit is obtained by combining fundamental units.
rubric.how: State that derived units are formed by combining base units through multiplication or division.

rubric.why: The newton is a derived SI unit of force.
rubric.how: Name the newton.

rubric.why: Any valid second derived unit earns credit.
rubric.how: Name a second derived unit, such as the joule or pascal.

modelAnswer: Derived units are the units formed by combining base units through multiplication or division.
Two examples are the newton (N) and the joule (J).

items.followUp: What is the least count of a screw gauge?

rubric.why: The least count describes the smallest measurable interval.
rubric.description: Identifies the least count as the smallest measurable value.
rubric.how: State that it is the smallest measurement an instrument can measure.

rubric.why: The definition must apply specifically to the instrument asked about.
rubric.description: Relates the definition to vernier callipers.
rubric.how: Specify that this smallest measurement is the one measurable by vernier callipers.

modelAnswer: The least count of vernier callipers is the smallest measurement that can be measured accurately with them.
It is equal to the difference between one main scale division and one vernier scale division.

rubric.why: Uniform velocity requires equal displacement in equal time intervals.
rubric.how: State that equal displacements are covered in equal intervals of time.

rubric.why: Velocity is a vector, so its direction must also be specified and remain unchanged.
rubric.how: State that the displacement is in a particular direction.

modelAnswer: A body has uniform velocity when it covers equal displacements in equal intervals of time in a particular direction.

items.followUp: A body of mass 5 kg moves with a velocity of 3 m/s. Find its momentum.

rubric.why: Momentum is defined as the product of mass and velocity.
rubric.how: Write momentum = mass × velocity, or p = mv.

rubric.why: The SI unit must be stated correctly.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of momentum.
rubric.how: State the SI unit as kg m/s (or N s).

modelAnswer: Momentum is the product of the mass of a body and its velocity: p = mv.
Its SI unit is kilogram metre per second (kg m/s).

items.followUp: Explain the difference between the centre of mass and the centre of gravity of a body.

rubric.why: The centre of mass represents the distribution of a body's mass.
rubric.how: State that it is the point at which the whole mass of the body may be considered concentrated.

rubric.why: The centre of gravity represents the point of application of the body's weight.
rubric.how: State that it is the point at which the whole weight of the body may be considered to act.

modelAnswer: The centre of mass is the point at which the whole mass of a body may be considered to be concentrated.
The centre of gravity is the point at which the whole weight of a body may be considered to act.
